# Model card: score projection

<!-- Generated by `criciq-ml report` from the model registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Version** 1.0.0 · **data** 2026-09-17.103eadea · served model trained on 2011-2026 (1,516 complete first innings, 187,565 match states)

## What it does

During a first innings of a T20 match (Big Bash League, Pakistan Super League, Caribbean Premier League, SA20; one model fitted on all of them at once), estimates the distribution of the final total after every ball: the median, an 80% range and the chance of passing any total. Chases are not projected, because a chase stops at its target (the win probability covers them). Outputs are model estimates of historical patterns, not predictions of live matches, and not for betting.

## How it works

- **Target:** the runs still to come, divided by what the scoring era would expect from the balls left (a rolling scoring rate of the competition). One model then stays valid from 2011 to 2026, while average first-innings totals rose by about 30 runs, and across competitions that score at different rates.
- **Model:** LightGBM quantile regression at the 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90 and 95% levels. Crossing quantiles are sorted.
- **Calibration:** conformal, per level. Each level is shifted by the matching quantile of its errors on held-out years, so that about that share of totals falls below it. The served model is calibrated on out-of-fold predictions for 2025, 2026.
- **P(total ≥ X)** is read off a piecewise-linear CDF through the quantiles. The CDF starts at the current score and ends a little beyond the 95% quantile.
- Rain-shortened innings are excluded from training and evaluation and are not projected.

**Features:** Legal balls bowled; Balls remaining; Wickets lost; Runs above the era's par for this stage; Run rate relative to the era's scoring rate; Runs in the last 12 legal balls; Wickets in the last 12 legal balls; Batters at the crease: career strike rate; Batters at the crease: career average; Batters at the crease: balls faced so far.

## Evaluation protocol

- **Tune** on 2021-2022, with candidates trained on years up to 2020.
- **Calibrate** on 2023-2024.
- **Test** on 2025-2026, touched once.
- No year does two jobs.
- Splits are calendar years of the match date (cut-offs on 1 January), so a BBL season that spans the new year falls on both sides of one.

The Brier score averages P(total ≥ X) for X in 160, 180, 200, 220. Bias is the median minus the actual total; positive means the projection ran high.

## Rolling-origin backtest

For each year *s*: fit on years before *s - 2*, calibrate on *s - 2* and *s - 1*, test on *s*. This doubles as the **bias check**, a watch on the drift in scoring across eras.

| Year | Innings | Mean total | 80% coverage | Median error | Par median error | Bias |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | 81 | 160.3 | 81.3% | 14.22 | 14.00 | -1.46 |
| 2017 | 88 | 156.3 | 81.1% | 14.38 | 14.90 | +6.56 |
| 2018 | 109 | 160.6 | 75.3% | 16.03 | 16.55 | +0.46 |
| 2019 | 126 | 161.5 | 80.3% | 15.05 | 15.05 | +1.56 |
| 2020 | 116 | 156.7 | 78.2% | 16.71 | 17.84 | +3.01 |
| 2021 | 128 | 169.0 | 79.8% | 15.12 | 15.59 | -6.19 |
| 2022 | 117 | 167.1 | 83.5% | 14.69 | 15.16 | +0.15 |
| 2023 | 149 | 171.3 | 75.5% | 16.62 | 17.27 | -0.57 |
| 2024 | 134 | 170.0 | 79.5% | 16.21 | 17.14 | +1.36 |
| 2025 | 141 | 172.3 | 80.0% | 16.47 | 17.68 | -1.03 |
| 2026 | 121 | 168.3 | 78.4% | 17.16 | 18.69 | +3.69 |

The projection beats par on median error in 9 of 11 years. Bias ranges from -6.2 to +6.6 runs. The scoring-era adjustment keeps it from drifting in one direction, but a single year can run a few runs high or low.

## Feature selection

Each candidate group was added to the served features and scored by rolling origin on 2016-2024, never on the test years.

None improved the pinball loss by more than 0.01 runs (well inside year-to-year noise), so the served model leaves them out.

| Variant | Pinball | Median error |
|---|---|---|
| Served features | 4.514 | 15.55 |
| + Batting still to come (career averages) | 4.509 | 15.55 |
| + Bowling still to come (career economy, 4-over quotas) | 4.557 | 15.70 |
| + Venue scoring index | 4.546 | 15.63 |
| + The competition's scoring rate | 4.615 | 15.85 |
| + International cricket | 4.514 | 15.55 |

## Limitations

- The range is calibrated on average over all balls, so coverage varies by phase: powerplay 77.0%, middle 82.1%, death 78.1% on the test years.
- Weather, pitch and team news are not in the data. The model knows the era, not the venue or the day.
- Innings reduced by rain are not projected.
